claims.text: FeNiCoCrAl-based high-entropy alloys are used as intermediate layers in plasma-facing reactor components.
Laser surface remelting followed by stress-relief treatment can reengineer the microstructure of FeNiCoCrAl-based high-entropy alloys.
The proposed processing produces uniformly aligned, elongated columnar grains.
The proposed processing produces highly coherent grain boundaries.
A laser power of approximately 300 W and scanning speed of approximately 10 mm/s constitute suitable optimized remelting parameters for this alloy.
In-situ monitoring can ensure uniform melting and rapid solidification during laser surface remelting.
Controlled rapid solidification and epitaxial solidification promote aligned columnar grain formation.
Aligned columnar grains with coherent boundaries reduce phonon scattering.
Reduced phonon scattering enhances thermal conduction in the FeNiCoCrAl-based alloy.
The stress-relief treatment minimizes residual stresses generated by laser surface remelting.
Minimizing residual stress prevents the enhanced thermal pathways from compromising long-term mechanical integrity under thermal cycling and cyclic loading.
The treated alloy will exhibit approximately 20% higher thermal conductivity than an as-cast or conventionally heat-treated baseline.
The treated alloy will maintain creep resistance similar to the baseline.
The treated alloy will maintain fatigue resistance similar to the baseline.
The predicted thermal and mechanical performance will hold between 300 and 600 °C under plasma-simulated cyclic mechanical loading.
Departures from the proposed laser parameters may reduce the thermal-conductivity enhancement or structural integrity.
Incomplete stress relief may reduce the thermal-conductivity enhancement or structural integrity.
